streams.the_prediction_exists_and_is_NOT_the_ans: Measured on a fixture carrying the same four paths: route `crewing-635-single-user`, status pass, changed files 4, protected 0, release false, comparison triple-dot, 19 harness commands all `not_run`, exit 0, and 0.04-0.06 s over three runs. That is a PREDICTION about a fixture, not a verdict about the vehicle, and the driver treats it as such: if the real route or file count differs, it prints a FINDING and still closes cleanly, because the stage succeeded in MEASURING. Failing the stage there would be the wrong shape - it would turn an unexpected measurement into a broken instrument, and the push decision does not belong inside this script.
streams.what_this_measurement_does_NOT_establish: All 19 harness commands print `not_run`, so this certifies ROUTE, SCOPE, protected-path touches and release-sensitivity - and NOT that the harnesses pass. That caveat has to travel with the number every time it is quoted. Two further limits worth carrying: one of the 19, `shared_host_runtime_isolation`, would run OUTSIDE this worktree entirely (in skipi-plugins/_host-runtime) if it ever ran, which is one reason not to run them here; and the route's allowlist includes src-tauri/Cargo.{toml,lock}, which are release-sensitive and blocked for a non-release task - so a clean route is not permission to touch them.
streams.the_flag_that_makes_this_stage_not_read_: The coordinator's finding, and he was right: `verify --json <path>` WRITES that file and calls `mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` on its parent (bin/skipi-guard 1149, 816-817, 633-637). Omit the flag and `verify` writes nothing at all - its body, lines 664-821, contains no other write primitive, which I checked by scanning that range rather than trusting the function's reputation. I keep the flag because the machine-readable verdict IS this stage's evidence, and I put the path INSIDE the declared log directory which the driver creates first, so write_json's mkdir is a no-op on an already-declared subtree. Worth recording the contrast he also measured: for `pre-push-ref` `--json` DEFAULTS to /tmp/skipi-guard-pre-push-<home>.json (853), while `verify` has no default - so the same flag name is opt-in on one subcommand and unavoidable on the other.
streams.why_verify_and_not_pre_push_ref: `pre_push_ref` does `git worktree add` into the SHARED gitdir (bin/skipi-guard:865) and `shutil.rmtree` (894), and calls verify with run_harness=True, executing harnesses in other repositories. Both primitives appear ONLY in that function; `verify` occupies 664-821 and contains neither - established by the function's line boundaries, not by the absence of the words nearby. And because the commit now exists, no fixture stand-in is needed: earlier in this task the route had to be predicted on a fixture precisely because `pre-push-ref` needs a sha that did not yet exist. The real object can now be measured directly, which is strictly better evidence.
streams.rc_1_is_a_verdict_not_a_failure: `verify` returns `0 if result["status"] == "pass" else 1` (line 820). So the driver maps 0 to pass, 1 to fail, and 2-or-more to an instrument failure, and keeps them apart. Conflating them cuts both ways: a refused route would be reported as a broken tool, or a broken tool as a clean route. Drilled with a stub guard exiting 2: exit 10, 'an INSTRUMENT failure, not a verdict'.
streams.the_stage_5_debt_is_PAID_and_drilled_on_: Stage 5's precondition pinned the ref COUNT (149), which the coordinator flagged as my own instrument applied inconsistently - I had already replaced a count with a name set twelve lines below, after the count cried FINDING over a merely re-packed ref. Here the precondition pins the SORTED NAME LIST in a declared sidecar (/home/linux/Developer/skipi-crewing/scratchpad/crewing-898/coord/refnames-s6.txt, sha256 de27f05ff072f1fd4476e3810186653a254e9c015575312b2f43efcd11d42297, 149 names, verified sorted and duplicate-free) and compares it with `comm`, reporting ADDED and GONE BY NAME. Drilled on the exact case the count is blind to: a SWAP - one ref deleted and one added, count identical at 3 = 3, set different - and the predicate stopped at exit 8 naming both sides: 'added [refs/remotes/origin/other2] gone [refs/remotes/origin/spare]'. A plain addition drills it too (exit 8, named), but the swap is the one that proves the replacement was worth making. The debt's removal criterion is therefore met in the same driver that declared it.
streams.a_drill_of_mine_that_was_illegal_and_how: My first attempt at the swap drill deleted refs/remotes/origin/HEAD, which made `git rev-parse origin/main` unresolvable - it echoes its input back, so the variable held the literal string 'origin/main' and an EARLIER gate fired (exit 7) before the predicate under test was ever reached. The output looked like a failure of the thing I was testing and was not. Repaired the fixture, added a spare ref so a swap could use a non-load-bearing name, re-pinned, re-established a clean baseline FIRST, and only then mutated. Same lesson as the no-op sed earlier in this task: a drill must be a LEGAL mutation, and a clean baseline immediately before it is what tells a real catch from collateral damage.
streams.a_process_error_of_mine_with_no_damage_m: Reporting it because stray execution near the vehicle must not be hidden. Building this driver I ran a python generator inside a shell heredoc whose delimiter was PYEOF - the same token appears inside the driver text being generated, so the outer heredoc terminated early and a few lines of the driver's body executed as shell. My own note says to build files with python rather than shell heredocs, and I broke it. Measured consequences, not assumed: the file was never created; the stray `> /verify.stdout` redirect failed with Permission denied so the guard never ran; `say` was undefined so those lines were no-ops. Verified afterwards - worktree HEAD e5132934 and porcelain empty, origin/main f145c601, canonical 0 tracked, `worktree list` 86 lines, no stray file at /, no stage-route directory and no guard-verify.json. The driver was then written with a single Write call instead, and the generator pattern retired for this class of file. Unique delimiters where a heredoc is unavoidable.
